newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom takes key step toward privatisation.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom takes key step toward privatisation.

text.p: State-owned telecommunications operator France Telecom became a public corporation on Tuesday, paving the way for its partial privatisation in 1997.

Declaring its aim of becoming a "French champion" worldwide, it said the change in status, resulting from a law passed last July, marked "an important step" in getting ready for full liberalisation of the European telecommunications market in 1998.

France Telecom SA, the world's fourth biggest telecoms operator, will have a share capital of 25 billion francs ($4.8 billion), comprising one billion shares carrying a nominal value of 25 francs each.

The government, which has pledged to retain 51 percent of the telecoms operator and set aside a maximum extra 10 percent for staff, hopes to raise 25 billion francs from the sale in the spring of a stake in France Telecom.
The planned float is one of a raft of share offerings in Europe by state-controlled telecoms companies in the countdown toward full competition.
The partial sale is to be made in two tranches and could help restore the centre-right government's privatisation drive following a couple of embarrassing setbacks.
Recently, the goverment had to suspend the sales of state electronics company Thomson and regional banking network CIC in the face of stiff political, trade union and staff opposition.
The sale of the first tranche of France Telecom was expected to start in April but published reports now suggest it may be held between May and mid-June.
Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said in October that 20 percent would be sold off in the first tranche, but the finance ministry said later the amount had not yet been fixed.

If the 20 percent figure is confirmed, around 200 million shares could be offered in the first sell-off. They would have to be priced at around 125 francs per share for the government to achieve its target of raising 25 billion francs.
That sum would largely cover the government's goal of raising 27 billion francs from privatisation receipts in 1997.

Analysts have said the feverish investor scramble for the monster first $13 billion tranche of Deutsche Telekom shares in November bodes well for France Telecom's flotation as well as for the sale of Italy's STET.
France Telecom is valued at 100-200 billion francs.

The wide range is partly because the interconnection charges -- the prices which France Telecom can charge its future rival telecommunications operators in France for the use of its network -- have yet to be agreed.

France Telecom, facing competition from French utility Cie Generale des Eaux in the telecommunications field, said it was confident it would be "the leading French player" in the global telecommunications market. ($1=5.225 French Franc)
